Gagner par le combat : déployer vite bea: Win through combat: deploy lots of cheap creatures fast and hit before the table is set up. In multiplayer (40 life per opponent), you need a low mana curve, protection and a way to rebuild after a board wipe.
Jeu flexible : survivre au début de part: Flexible play: survive the early game, then build up mana and cards with value engines and some interaction, adapting to the table. Value alone does not win: you need real win conditions.
Neutraliser les menaces de la table (con: Neutralize the table's threats (counterspells, removal, board wipes) while keeping card advantage, then close out with a few resilient threats. Against three opponents drawing cards, removal matters as much as counterspells; the trap is dominating without ever finishing.
Assembler quelques cartes précises dont: Assemble a few specific cards whose interaction wins the game on the spot (infinite mana or damage loop, alternate win), using tutors and card draw to find them. Fragile against removal and counterspells: you need redundancy and protection.
Entre aggro et contrôle : poser des mena: Between aggro and control: deploy efficient threats, then make opponents waste time and mana (bounce, cheap counterspells) to extend your lead. In Commander, mass bounce pays off more than targeted bounce, and you need threats to take advantage of it.
Poser des permanents qui taxent ou bloqu: Play permanents that tax or lock opponents' resources (mana, lands, spells) while shielding yourself better than the table, then win once the lock is in place. Trap: a lock without a fast win condition makes the game endless. Close to Prison, which aims for more precise locks.
Verrouiller le jeu adverse par des effet: Lock down opponents with hard effects: stop them from untapping their permanents (Stasis), casting cheap spells (Trinisphere) or attacking (Ensnaring Bridge). Close to Stax, but with precise locks and a win plan the lock does not hinder.
Se rendre peu attractif à attaquer sans: Make yourself unattractive to attack without stopping others from playing: a tax per attacking creature, attacker limits, deterrent effects. You build value behind these defenses and win late, outside of combat. Vulnerable to enchantment removal and fast combos.
Empiler équipements, auras et bonus de p: Stack equipment, auras and power boosts on a single creature, often the commander, with evasion and protection, to deal 21 commander damage to each opponent, one at a time. A single removal or exile undoes several turns of investment.
Storm est un mot-clé : quand on lance le: Storm is a keyword: when you cast the spell, it is copied once for each spell cast earlier in the turn. The deck chains rituals, card draw, cost reducers and tutors to raise that count, then finishes with a storm spell (damage, life loss, mill). Fragile against counterspells and discard.
Pas de synergie centrale ni de plan uniq: No central synergy or single plan: the deck gathers the most powerful and versatile cards in the commander's colors (acceleration, tutors, card draw, removal). Games end in many ways, so still include a few ways to close them out.
Une boîte à outils : des réponses ciblée: A toolbox: targeted answers (removal, counterspells, protection, card draw, finishers) and tutors, often for creatures, to find the right tool at the right time. The deck adapts to the table and wins through combat, combo or direct damage.
Un deck, surtout vert, qui accélère son: A mostly green deck that ramps its mana early (mana creatures, ramp) to drop big creatures in the first turns and overwhelm opponents in combat. Its weak point is a stalled board: it needs evasion and removal.
Un deck de petites créatures bon marché: A deck of cheap small creatures (often 1 or 2 mana, mostly white), deployed in numbers to swarm the table, then exploited through synergies: enter-the-battlefield triggers, sacrifice, card draw, mass damage. Vulnerable to board wipes.
Un deck qui mise sur le hasard et l'impr: A deck that bets on luck and unpredictability: dice, coin flips, card swaps, random effects, forced attacks. It wins by upending the board rather than through a linear plan, and plays best after talking it over with the table (rule 0).
Un deck qui gagne en orientant les autre: A deck that wins by steering the other players: votes, deals, gifts or removal threats to decide who attacks whom, often with the monarch or goad. It requires keeping your promises and punishing traitors.
Un deck qui aide toute la table (pioche,: A deck that helps the whole table (card draw, mana, life gain, creatures) instead of seeking a personal edge. These gifts win allies and deflect aggression; some decks aim for a real win, others mostly for chaos.
Faire perdre de la vie à toute la table: Make the whole table lose life bit by bit through mass effects (damage on each draw, land or spell; sometimes symmetrical, yourself included). You win by attrition while protecting yourself better (lifelink, prevention), but the deck quickly becomes the target.
Un deck de petites créatures bon marché: A deck of cheap small creatures whose effect hampers opponents: taxes, bans, limits on drawing or searching. Unlike Stax, it keeps up pressure in combat to win. Vulnerable to board wipes, it needs card draw.
Un deck qui produit bien plus de mana qu: A deck that makes far more mana than it needs (mana creatures and rocks, land ramp) to cast very expensive spells (often 7 mana or more), X spells or Eldrazi. Unlike regular ramp, the excess mana is the main plan.
Accélérer son mana au-delà d'un terrain: Accelerate your mana beyond one land per turn: spells that fetch lands, mana creatures, mana rocks. You cast your big cards earlier, or even several spells per turn. A balanced deck usually runs about ten sources; too much ramp leaves you with nothing to cast.
Deck bâti sur les éphémères et les ritue: A deck built on instants and sorceries: lots of cheap spells and creatures or permanents that trigger on each spell cast (tokens, damage, copies, cost reduction). You win with tokens, small creatures, direct damage or a combo. Often blue-red.
Jouer des contresorts, qui annulent un s: Play counterspells, which cancel an opponent's spell as it is cast, to stop a combo or a threat from resolving. In multiplayer each counterspell stops only one spell, and you need to keep mana open during other players' turns.
Piocher au-delà de la pioche du tour pou: Draw beyond your draw step so you never depend on the top card: repeatable engines, one-off draw spells, creatures that draw when they enter. Not to be confused with cantrips, which only replace themselves; aim for about ten sources of card advantage.
Sorts très bon marché qui piochent une c: Very cheap spells that draw a card on top of their effect, so they replace themselves: you gain efficiency and selection rather than card advantage. They let you cast many spells per turn to feed cards that reward each spell (spellslinger).
Des sorts dont l'effet dépend d'un X pay: Spells whose effect depends on an X paid in mana: the more you spend, the bigger the effect. The deck therefore seeks lots of mana, often in green and blue, plus cards that copy or amplify X spells.
Cartes avec flash, lançables à tout mome: Cards with flash, castable any time you could cast an instant: a surprise blocker after attacks are declared, or a creature dropped at the end of an opponent's turn to attack right after. Cards like Vedalken Orrery give flash to every spell.
Dégâts directs hors combat : sorts qui b: Direct damage outside of combat: spells that hit any target, and permanents that deal damage on each event (a creature entering, a sacrifice, a spell cast). You kill creatures or drain opponents' life, harder in Commander with 40 life each.
Gagner de la vie à répétition, par tous: Gain life repeatedly, by any means (lifelink, triggers, healing spells), to power cards that react to each gain: +1/+1 counters, card draw, tokens, a final drain. Life also serves as a resource to spend.
Faire perdre de la vie aux adversaires h: Make opponents lose life outside of combat, often gaining as much: one-shot drains or repeated triggers on each creature that dies. You win through life loss rather than attacks, mostly in black.
Envoyer les cartes du dessus de la bibli: Send the top cards of opponents' libraries to the graveyard until an opponent has to draw from an empty library and loses. Against three 99-card libraries, you need massive effects (half the library), doublers or effects repeated every turn.
Mettre les cartes du dessus de sa propre: Put the top cards of your own library into your graveyard to turn them into a resource: reanimation, casting cards from the graveyard, cards that count the graveyard. Milling is fuel here, not a win condition; opposing graveyard exile is the big danger.
Faire défausser les adversaires pour les: Make opponents discard to deprive them of resources before they are played, often with cards that punish each discard or an empty hand. You need closing cards (damage, drain), or the game bogs down.
Effets « wheel » : chaque joueur défauss: "Wheel" effects: each player discards their hand and draws a new one, often of seven cards (after Wheel of Fortune). The deck refills faster than the table, disrupts big opposing hands and exploits the draws and discards with trigger cards.
Gagner avec les cartes des adversaires :: Win with your opponents' cards: take control of their creatures or artifacts (Control Magic), borrow them for a turn (Threaten) or cast their exiled cards. Temporary effects pair with sacrifice to get rid of the creature before it goes back.
Renvoyer des permanents en main : les si: Return permanents to hand: your own to replay their enter-the-battlefield effects, opponents' to gain tempo, get around indestructible and make tokens disappear. Bounce does not win on its own: it helps you strike or buy the time you need.
Thème bâti sur la zone d'exil : surtout: A theme built on the exile zone: mostly playing cards from exile (impulse draw, suspend, adventure, stolen cards), which gives card advantage and often Treasure tokens, more rarely exile as permanent removal.
Détruire les terrains adverses pour étou: Destroy opponents' lands to choke their mana: targeted (Stone Rain) or mass destruction (Armageddon, Ruination), with land recursion and ramp to recover before everyone else. A strongly frowned-upon strategy: check with the table first.
Sorts donnant un ou plusieurs tours supp: Spells that grant one or more extra turns: another untap, another attack and one more draw to end the game or chain a combo. The deck replays these spells through recursion or copying, up to an infinite loop. Without a win plan, you become the table's enemy.
Forcer les créatures adverses à attaquer: Force opposing creatures to attack: goad (they must attack each combat if able, and not you, until your next turn) or static effects. The deck profits from the chaos (drain, card draw) and protects itself from retaliation.
Créer beaucoup de jetons de créature, le: Create lots of creature tokens, multiply them with doublers, then turn them into damage with mass effects. Numbers hold up against targeted removal, but not against board wipes.
Variante du sacrifice : des créatures-fo: A sacrifice variant: fodder creatures (often tokens), a way to sacrifice them at will and cards that trigger on each death (drain, card draw, Treasure). Opposing board wipes feed the engine; the deck wins by draining opponents' life.
Sacrifier des permanents (créatures, jet: Sacrifice permanents (creatures, tokens, artifacts, sometimes lands) to get value from them: card draw, mana, damage, counters. You need fodder, sacrifice outlets and cards that profit from it. Broader than aristocrats, which focus on draining.
Remplir son cimetière de grosses créatur: Fill your graveyard with big creatures (discard, loot effects, putting cards into the graveyard from the library), then bring them back to the battlefield for 1 to 3 mana. A big tempo gain, but fragile against graveyard exile (Relic of Progenitus).
Faire du cimetière une seconde réserve d: Make the graveyard a second card pool: you fill it (discard, self-mill), then recast spells (flashback), get cards back or exile cards to reduce costs (delve). Broader than reanimator; vulnerable to graveyard exile (Rest in Peace, Bojuka Bog).
Exiler ses permanents puis les remettre: Exile your permanents, then return them to the battlefield right away to retrigger their enter-the-battlefield effects (card draw, mana, removal, tokens): you win by attrition, and an instant-speed blink dodges removal. Note: the permanent comes back fresh (counters and auras lost, exiled token gone).
Copier des créatures, les siennes ou cel: Copy creatures, yours or your opponents', to repeat their enter-the-battlefield effects or benefit from the most powerful one on the battlefield; in singleton, this gives you several copies of your best cards. A copier does, however, depend on a good target already in play.
Poser des marqueurs +1/+1 sur ses créatu: Put +1/+1 counters on your creatures to grow them, mostly in green and white. You amplify with effects that add or double them (Hardened Scales adds 1 counter, Doubling Season doubles), then win with an oversized board or bonuses triggered by counters.
Mot-clé qui permet de choisir n'importe: A keyword that lets you choose any number of permanents and/or players with counters and give each one more of every kind already there (+1/+1, loyalty, poison, charge…). Used to speed up planeswalker ultimates, grow creatures or poison players.
Mot-clé infect : les dégâts d'une source: The infect keyword: damage from a source with infect does not remove life, it gives players poison counters (10 = loss) and creatures permanent -1/-1 counters. The deck lines up infect creatures, power pumps and proliferate.
Gagner en empoisonnant les adversaires :: Win by poisoning opponents: a player with 10 or more poison counters loses the game, whatever their life total, and poison is almost never removed. Sources: infect, toxic, poisonous or direct effects, often amplified by proliferate.
Un deck rempli d'artefacts qui se renfor: A deck full of artifacts that strengthen each other: cost reduction, recycling and sacrifice, enter-the-battlefield effects and tokens, to deploy big threats early. Fragile to mass artifact destruction (Bane of Progress, Vandalblast), which also takes out mana artifacts.
Équiper ses créatures (en phase principa: Equip your creatures (at sorcery speed, paying the equip cost) with equipment that grants bonuses, evasion, protection or card draw, often Voltron-style on the commander. Unlike auras, equipment stays on the battlefield if the creature dies and can be re-equipped elsewhere.
Enchanter ses créatures avec des auras (: Enchant your creatures with auras (bonuses, protection) to turn them into threats. Risk: if the creature dies or leaves the battlefield, the aura goes to the graveyard (two cards lost for one). Umbras (which survive destruction) and aura-related card draw make up for it.
Deck centré sur les enchantements (auras: A deck focused on enchantments (auras, sagas, enchantment creatures) with "enchantresses" that draw a card each time an enchantment is cast or enters the battlefield (constellation). Ramp and protection handle the setup, tokens or life gain close it out. Vulnerable to enchantment wipes.
Deck qui joue beaucoup de planeswalkers: A deck that plays many planeswalkers and activates their loyalty abilities each turn to draw, make mana, create tokens or control the table. They draw attacks; unlike Superfriends, the commander is not necessarily built around them.
Archétype bâti autour des planeswalkers: An archetype built around planeswalkers: you protect them (attack taxes, blockers, mass removal) and speed up their loyalty with proliferate and counter doublers to reach their ultimates. A slow plan, and planeswalkers draw attacks.
Les Véhicules sont des artefacts qui dev: Vehicles are artifacts that become artifact creatures until end of turn when you tap creatures with enough total power (Crew N), even ones that arrived this turn. You need creatures to crew them, and artifact removal threatens them.
Landfall se déclenche chaque fois qu'un: Landfall triggers each time a land enters the battlefield under your control: tokens, cards, mana or bonuses depending on the card. The deck plays more lands (Exploration, Cultivate, recursion) and creatures or enchantments that profit from them.
Deck qui tire sa valeur des terrains eux: A deck that draws value from the lands themselves rather than from spells alone: extra land drops, lands replayed from the graveyard, sacrificed lands or powerful utility lands, often with Landfall. Broader than Landfall, it wins by piling up value: tokens, cards, giant creatures.
Créer des jetons Trésor : des artefacts: Create Treasure tokens: artifacts you tap and sacrifice to add one mana of any color, just once. This disposable mana lets you cast big spells early, and cards that reward artifacts, sacrifice or tokens turn it into damage or advantage.
Créer des jetons Nourriture : des artefa: Create Food tokens: artifacts you tap and sacrifice, for 2 mana, to gain 3 life. The life gain is secondary: the deck mostly makes them to sacrifice them and trigger synergies (sacrifice, card draw, tokens, combos).
Créer des jetons Sang : un artefact qui,: Create Blood tokens: an artifact that, for 1 mana, by tapping, discarding a card and sacrificing itself, lets you draw a card (you discard before drawing). Tied to vampires (mostly black and red), Blood fuels sacrifice and drain effects.
Le monarque pioche une carte au début de: The monarch draws a card at the beginning of their own end step; as soon as a creature deals combat damage to the monarch, its controller becomes the monarch. The deck takes the crown, then keeps it with blockers, tokens and pillow fort.
Les malédictions sont des Auras qui s'at: Curses are Auras that attach to a player and hinder them. The deck stacks them on an opponent and adds enchantment synergies and recursion from the graveyard. A slow plan: each curse targets only one player.
Donner à un adversaire un permanent nuis: Give an opponent a harmful permanent you control, with Donate or Harmless Offering: control changes, not ownership. Typical: Illusions of Grandeur, which gains you 20 life, then makes its holder lose 20 when it leaves the battlefield. A political game.
